topics.topic: Bootstrap command outcome, exit code, and permitted output for runtime-settings failure
questions: Which declared command outcome and exit code result when `load_runtime_settings` refuses the environment, and what may the command print?
Which BootstrapCommandOutcome and exit code does the CLI produce when load_runtime_settings rejects the environment?
Which closed BootstrapCommandOutcome and exit code represent a runtime-settings failure?

quotes:
One message per outcome on the terminal; the password or its hash is never
echoed, printed or logged.

Each refusal is its exit code. A configuration or storage failure is none of
the four outcomes: the operation raises it and returns no exit code, and the
failure status the host process then ends with is outside the closed
contract of A29.
judgement.why: State 5 states that configuration failure is not a BootstrapCommandOutcome, escapes without a command exit code, and remains subject to the terminal-output secrecy rule.

topics.topic: Caller and execution context of decode_recognition_publication
questions: Who calls `decode_recognition_publication`, and for an HTTP expense request does that call occur before authorization, after authorization, or only on a separate non-HTTP path?

Which named module or operation receives the undecoded OCR payload and calls decode_recognition_publication, and how does that path obtain the authorized staff context, project and allocations required for expense creation?

Who calls decode_recognition_publication outside the HTTP route, and how does that caller obtain the authenticated staff context, project and allocations required to continue into create_expense_from_recognition?

quotes:
`boundary:ocr_service`: the confirmed recognition the external OCR service
publishes, before it reaches the consumer. The HTTP route decodes its request
body with its own model check; the consumer checks the version again.

The `PortalStore`, an `AuthorizedProjectContext`, one
`ConfirmedRecognitionPublication` and the operator's `AllocationInstruction`
list.
judgement.why: State 5 separates the OCR boundary's payload decoder from the HTTP route and states that only the API calls expense creation with the authorized context and allocations.

topics.topic: Whether RuntimeSettings is captured once or reloaded for each Registry call
questions: Does `once` mean once for the process, or once during initial application construction while later Registry calls reread the environment through `load_runtime_settings`?
After service start, does registry_gateway reuse the start-up settings or reload the environment for every Registry call?
Is the environment captured once for the running service, or re-read for every Registry call?

quotes:
`module:runtime_settings` owns reading the environment, once: the closed table
`config.runtime_environment_variables`, defaults, normalization and the
startup checks (A30), into `RuntimeSettings`.

`registry_gateway`
  takes the Registry URL from the `registry_base_url` field of the
  `RuntimeSettings` that `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at
  each Registry call: the call reads and validates the environment again
  through `runtime_settings`, the same environment the start validated, and
  no settings object is handed to the gateway or cached by it (A6, A30; owner 2026-11-09: the Registry URL is read only through
  `runtime_settings`, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11).
judgement.divergence: One implementation retains and uses the start-time Registry URL, while another reloads the environment and uses the current URL for every Registry call; the request caller and the Registry endpoints observe which service receives the request.
judgement.why: State 4 says the environment is read once, while State 3 expressly requires another complete environment read at every Registry call.

topics.topic: Whether service start-up rejects an unusable but nonblank Registry URL
questions: Must start-up reject a nonblank but unusable Registry URL, or accept every nonblank value and leave URL-form validation to each Registry call?
Does an unusable but nonblank Registry URL stop start-up, or is it accepted at start and rejected only when a Registry call is made?
Does an unusable but nonblank Registry URL stop service start-up, or is it accepted until a Registry call fails?

quotes:
`capability:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings` reads and validates the
   environment variables of A30; a missing, malformed or inconsistent one (a
   wildcard host or origin, binary bounds out of order) stops the start
   before any request is served. The Registry URL is one of them since the
   owner's decision of 2026-11-09 (A6, A30): the service does not start
   without it.

The start-up check refuses only a missing value or
one that is empty or whitespace only, tested on the value as supplied (the
row's normalization is `none`); which values the gateway accepts as a base URL and how it joins them
with the request paths stay the accepted gateway's (note `_registry_url`,
the Registry path constants), carried to States 6–7.
judgement.divergence: One implementation rejects a nonblank malformed Registry URL during start-up, while another starts and defers rejection until a Registry call; the deployment operator and Registry-dependent caller observe the difference.
judgement.why: State 4 includes the Registry URL among values whose malformed form stops start-up, while State 2 says every nonblank form is accepted at start.

topics.topic: Translation of per-call runtime-settings reload failures into gateway and HTTP failures
questions: When the gateway's per-call `load_runtime_settings` fails after the service has started, which module translates that failure, which declared failure does the gateway produce, and which HTTP status results?

What failure does a Registry-dependent operation produce when the per-call load_runtime_settings fails because any required setting other than the Registry URL became missing or invalid after service start?

quotes: _registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the Registry deployment URL, which is the registry_base_url field of the RuntimeSettings that the imported load_runtime_settings returns when this function calls it, and MUST preserve that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request; it MUST NOT read the process environment itself. A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings.

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero, except in the two reads whose Errors say so:
judgement.why: The later notes require the gateway not to translate a load_runtime_settings refusal, and the public API convention maps that unclassified failure to HTTP 500 rather than Registry transport_error and 502.

topics.topic: Whether bootstrap rejects an unusable but nonblank Registry URL
questions: For the bootstrap command, what makes the Registry URL `invalid`: only missing, empty or whitespace-only input, or also a URL form the gateway cannot use?
Does the bootstrap command reject an unusable but nonblank Registry URL, even though it makes no Registry call?

quotes:
The command loads the same start-up table as the
   service, so a missing or invalid required variable — the Registry URL
   among them since 2026-11-09 (A30) — ends it before any store exists.

The start-up check refuses only a missing value or
one that is empty or whitespace only, tested on the value as supplied (the
row's normalization is `none`); which values the gateway accepts as a base URL and how it joins them
with the request paths stay the accepted gateway's (note `_registry_url`,
the Registry path constants), carried to States 6–7.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats an unusable nonblank Registry URL as an invalid required variable and stops before creating a store, while another accepts it and completes bootstrap because no Registry call occurs; the host operator and database observer notice whether the administrator exists.
judgement.why: The bootstrap flow says an invalid Registry URL ends the command, while A30 limits runtime-settings rejection of that URL to missing or blank values.
